subject: grayWolf
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: gray wolf standing alert.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
Looking at the render, I'm noting the muzzle appears too long and thin, more like a greyhound than a wolf, and the cream-colored lower jaw hangs oddly as if detached and slightly agape. The head also reads too small relative to the body, so it needs to be bulkier and more proportionate to match true wolf identity cues like the thick ruff and bushy tail.

The mane and ruff tufts are rendering as flat dark shard-like spikes rather than soft fur, giving an unwanted hedgehog/spiky look from the back and top views, and the collar strap floats oddly off the neck like a standalone ring rather than sitting naturally. The legs are also too long and thin with the cream lower portions making the body look tall and spindly, though the tail and hind thighs read fine. Overall the wolf is dwarfed by an oversized base (radius 1.28 vs. a body length of about 1.3), so I'm thinking I need to shrink the base to roughly 1.0 and reposition the props -- the obelisk, banner, and pine -- since the banner pole currently overlaps awkwardly with the pine and sits too close to the tail in the three-quarter view.

The obelisk is also occluding the muzzle from the three-quarter camera angle, so I need to shift it from its current front-left position back behind the wolf's side, while keeping the pine, banner, and front crystal placements roughly as they are since those read fine. For the head itself, my priority is fixing identity: I want to widen and shorten the muzzle with a cleaner closed jaw, adjusting the loft stations so the snout flares a bit wider near the base, narrows smoothly toward the tip, and ends sooner for a stockier, more wolf-like profile instead of the current long thin taper.

Now I'm tuning the jaw geometry to sit flush under the shortened muzzle so the mouth reads as closed rather than gapped, adjusting the jaw's vertical position and taper radii to match the new muzzle underside, then shifting the nose position and repainting thresholds (nose, cream muzzle, eye, cheek, whisker dot regions) so they still land correctly on the resized head, and finally re-checking the fang placement against the new muzzle-bottom height.

I'm repositioning the lip drape z-endpoints to follow the adjusted muzzle, moving the eye decal hit point and possibly enlarging the eyes slightly for visibility from the front. I'm also noticing the dorsal mane tufts render more like stegosaurus plates than fur spikes in the top view, so I'm considering thinning them out and making them lie flatter along the spine.

The ruff ring tufts at the neck are reading as thin spikes rather than a mane, so I want to widen them and angle them backward; meanwhile the collar loop placed at the neck is getting buried behind the ruff and chest tufts, so I'm thinking about relocating it lower or raising its lift so the pendant actually shows.

A bigger fix might be to scale down the whole base relative to the wolf, shrinking the lathe outline radii and rune ring plane by about 0.82x and repositioning the rocks and props inward accordingly.

I need to check the wolf's tail extent though — at the current base radius the tail tip would overhang the edge, so I'm adjusting the base center and radius to make sure the tail stays within bounds.

Checking if the obelisk placement at that corner position still fits within the decagon's apothem for the smaller radius — the base box might now poke outside the boundary, so I need to verify the clearance.

I need to figure out the camera's actual position relative to the wolf to know if the obelisk would be occluded—since the wolf's head points toward screen-left, that tells me which side the camera is viewing from.

Since the banner sits nearest the camera, I'm trying to triangulate the camera position - if it's on the +X +Z side, the wolf facing +Z would appear heading toward screen-right from that vantage.

Working through the vector math, I confirm the camera sits at the model's left-front, with +Z mapping to screen-left. That puts the obelisk at screen-x -1.5 (far left), the banner near-right at 1.05, and the pine far-right at 1.5 - so I need to position the obelisk away from the head to avoid occluding the face.

Checking the wolf head position against the obelisk's screen coordinates, I realize they're too close together, risking overlap with the neck. Since the front-view mapping is proving confusing to reason about cleanly, I decide to just place the obelisk on the far side behind the wolf instead, using the 3/4 camera's far-side coordinates so the wolf naturally occludes it rather than the reverse.

Still checking screen-space overlap between the muzzle and the obelisk at different z positions, trying to find a placement where the obelisk's width doesn't collide with the wolf's muzzle or neck silhouette.

I'm checking whether the obelisk placement overlaps the head or ears at various heights, and adjusting its position further back so it sits behind the torso instead, out of the face/head silhouette.

I'm also weighing alternative spots for the obelisk, pine tree, and banner to avoid overlapping the wolf's rump, tail, and hips from the 3/4 view, trying different x/z coordinates to keep each element visually separated.

Now I'm checking whether the obelisk would end up hidden behind the wolf in the front-facing camera view, and deciding that's acceptable since it's positioned to the left/back. I'm also reconsidering the crystals' placement near the front-right of the wolf, verifying their distance from center stays within the allowed radius.

I'm now adjusting the rocks and mounds, nudging several coordinates inward to keep them within the radius limit while avoiding overlap with the obelisk's base.

Repositioning the remaining mounds to avoid overlap, then adjusting the grass scatter filter radius to match the updated center point. I'm also checking the banner pole's position so it stays clear of the base edge while still hanging toward the correct side.

Next I check the pine tree placement—it's sitting too far out near the base edge, so I'm nudging its coordinates inward and shrinking its bottom tier radius slightly to keep it from overhanging, accepting a small overlap as a reasonable compromise.

I also check the wolf's tail and hind leg positions against the pine, confirming no conflict there, then weigh moving the banner nearer the camera so it naturally covers part of the wolf's rear torso and tail, which seems to work with the current render.

Adjusting the tail curve to a smoother downward path with four points. Now checking body proportions — shoulder height and body depth look roughly realistic for a wolf, but the legs need to be chunkier and paws bigger to match the stylized Blizzard look.

Increasing leg segment radii and paw sizes for a sturdier build. The head also needs to be a bit oversized with bigger, broader ears, so I'm adjusting ear width, height, and base position to sit properly against the enlarged head.

Checking ear x-positioning and orientation on both sides, the cheek ruff tufts look fine as is, and I'll leave the dorsal tufts alone. The neck ring daggers should be widened for a shingled mane effect, keeping thickness the same, while the collar stays untouched.

The hip joint parenting is a bit odd but tolerable since only one root bone is allowed, and the floating crystal beside the obelisk can stay as is for now. I should bump the eye size up slightly to make them more visible from the front.

Checking the eye hit detection against the wider head taper, it should still register fine near the current z-position. I'm also considering enlarging the nose sphere slightly for a chunkier look, verifying the muzzle width accommodates it, and double-checking the jaw joint placement and aim target for the bite sweep.

I'll leave the jaw closed rather than posing it open, to avoid misaligning the lip geometry. Now I'm preparing the precise search-and-replace edits for the tail path and head loft block.

Writing edit search blocks...

Adjusting final station and headpaint threshold for the nose cutoff, then moving to check the jaw sweep curve definition.

Adjusting nose highlight position and starting the fang spike geometry...

Still adjusting fang placements and eye decal sizing...

I'm reworking the lip curve points with new z and y coordinates for a smoother contour, then moving on to extrude the ear tuft geometry.

Adjusting the ear extrusion sizes for outer and inner tufts, then tweaking the ring tuft calls to increase their sizes and adjust the color threshold condition.

Now I'm scaling up the leg sweep profiles for both front and hind legs, and enlarging the paw sphere's scale values for a bulkier look.

For the base, I'm shrinking the lathe outline points so the base radius narrows, and adjusting the snow ring profile points to match the new smaller scale proportionally.

Now I'm repositioning the ground mounds and rocks scattered around the scene, scaling their coordinates inward to fit the reduced base size while keeping their relative placement similar.

I'm removing the conflicting mound and repositioning elements to avoid overlap, shifting the banner and pole placement, adjusting a fourth mound near the pine so their spans don't collide, and nudging positions slightly to keep spacing clean.

Now I'm tightening the grass filter distance threshold and relocating the obelisk's base coordinates, checking that its corner distance from center stays within the allowed radius given its box half-diagonal.

Worried the wolf body will overlap visually with the obelisk since both are grayish tones; tried shifting the obelisk further right-front but that collides with the muzzle again, so better to keep it behind the wolf and maybe darken its contrast slightly. Moving on to defining the banner element now.

Adjusting banner, pine, and crystal coordinates...
